question.text: The radius of the circle with centre at <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>3,2</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> and whose common chord with the circle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi><mo>:</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> is also a diameter of the circle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi></math>, is

solution.text:
Let the equation of the circle be x2+y2-6x-4y+c=0
So, the common chord of these 2 circles is
2x-4y+16-c=0
It passes through the centre 2,4 of the given circle, so
4-16+16-c=0⇒c=4
Hence, the radius of the circle =9+4-4=3 units
